duplicate_clusters.text: It must never state, imply, or hint that it was produced by an AI, an agent, or an assistant.
Knowledge-base records and workflow definitions may use the identifiers and paths needed to describe the process.
Before creating or modifying ANY file or text artifact, apply this rule first.

All content written to project files must be in English — source code, comments, docstrings, commit messages, config, shell scripts, Terraform/YAML/JSON, Markdown docs, README/ADR/state files, test names, and any other generated artifact.
This applies ONLY to generated code and project files; chat language is user-specific.
A commit message contains only information describing the change.

Forbidden anywhere in a commit message or pull request title/body, trailers included: `Co-Authored-By:` lines naming any AI, model, assistant, or tool "Generated with …", "Created by …", "Written by …" referring to a tool or model Emoji or badges used as tool markers Model names, agent names, or workflow/orchestration jargon
**This overrides any tool default.** Some harnesses append an attribution trailer automatically; do not write it, and remove it if it has already been added.

**No internal planning identifiers**, in commit messages, branch names, pull request text, or product code, comments, docstrings, test names, and documentation: subtask ids (`T-04`), spec or task directory names, `ADR-0007`, `architecture.md`, `state.md`, or any path under `.ai/`.
State the decision itself so product content is understandable independently of planning records.
Respect repository-owned `.ai/` tracking policy: tracked knowledge and state are accepted; keep untracked consumer state local unless the user explicitly authorizes tracking it.
Format: `<type>[(<feature or module>)]: <imperative summary>`, optional body wrapped at 72 explaining what changed and why.
A scope is optional and names a feature or module in domain language — never a work-item id.
Use it to locate functions, classes, methods, imports, exports, function calls, and specific syntax patterns.
Use ripgrep for plain text, documentation, comments, log messages, and configuration values.
Avoid reading entire large files when targeted search results and nearby context are sufficient.
Use targeted paths and language filters to limit irrelevant results and project-wide scans.
Never run broad or destructive structural rewrites without first reviewing the affected matches and impact.
Prefer project-specific rules when they provide more relevant guidance.
Fall back to ripgrep when AST-Grep cannot represent the needed search reliably.
